titleEn: A Shot for Sheep, a Shot for Pipo!

pages.text: "Mom, who is that goat with a bag?" Pipo pointed beyond the wall. "The goat doctor who visits the sheep. Today sheep and Pipo each get one shot." His ears drooped. "M-me too?"
"No shot! I do not like pointy things!" He dashed behind the shed and hid with his back against its wall. "How much will that prick hurt...?" The thought made him shiver.
A sheep called baa loudly in the yard. His heart thumped. "The sheep hurts too... what if I cry?" He peeped through a gap in the wall.
Oh? The sheep that had received a shot jumped and ran happily. The goat doctor approached with the bag. "You must be Pipo. Did you see that sheep? Running even better after one prick!"

The doctor crouched beside him. "Brave little soldiers live inside your body. When wriggly germs arrive, your strength fades. A shot is medicine that strengthens the soldiers. A shot for sheep, a shot for Pipo!"
Pipo swallowed. "The soldiers... get stronger?" "Yes. With the medicine, they jump up and defeat germs," the doctor whispered. Mom came behind the shed and held his hand.
Pipo breathed deeply out and stretched his arm. Holding Mom's hand, he squeezed his eyes shut. Prick! "Oh? ...Oh? Not painful at all!" His eyes flew open.
In the yard, he crouched among sheep, hands at his chest. "I did not cry! The soldiers feel stronger." Sheep jumped around him.
Before the doctor, he showed three fingers. "One, a deep breath out! Two, arm stretched! Three, think of brave soldiers!" The doctor lifted the bag and laughed. "A shot for sheep, a shot for Pipo!"
On the hill, Pipo jumped with the sheep. One shot protected his body, so he felt no pain. He ran to Mom's lap and nestled in. "A shot for sheep, a shot for Pipo!"
